top_cited_works.title: Breakup of Round Nonturbulent Liquid Jets in Gaseous Crossflow
top_cited_works.abstract: An experimental investigation of the primary breakup of round nonturbulent liquid jets in gaseous crossflow is described. Pulsed shadowgraph and holograph observations were made to determine the following breakup properties: primary breakup regimes, conditions required for the onset of ligament and drop formation, ligament and drop sizes along the liquid surface, drop velocities after breakup, rates of liquid breakup along the liquid surface, conditions required for the breakup of the liquid column as a whole, and liquid column trajectories. These observations were made for round nonturbulent liquid jets in subsonic crossflow at normal temperature and pressure. The results suggest qualitative similarities between the primary breakup of nonturbulent round liquid jets in gaseous crossflow and the secondary breakup of drops subjected to shock wave disturbances. Phenomenological analyses were effective to help interpret and correlate the new measurements of the primary breakup properties of nonturbulent round liquid jets in gaseous crossflow. recent_works.title: Optimization of Low-Grade Solar Thermal Desalination Powerplant
recent_works.abstract: Abstract An optimized design for a solar-powered desalination plant is proposed in this study, motivated by the increasing demand for freshwater. The main objective of this paper is to investigate the viability of a Mechanical Vapor Compression (MVC) desalination system powered by a Regenerative Organic Rankine Cycle utilizing a low-grade solar thermal energy system within 200°C –400°C. The success criteria of the desalination plant are based on the recovery ratio, flow rate, and specific power consumption. The test matrix includes feed concentrations of up to 35 ppt and boiler temperatures ranging from 200 °C to 400 °C, typical of Low-grade solar collectors. Comparative analysis of power output for different cycles has been presented, and the results indicate that for heat sources below 400°C, the application of regenerative ORC is recommended. The results show that the Regenerative Rankine cycle can achieve a thermal efficiency of up to 33%. The study examined both compression and vacuum modes of the MVC desalination plant. It was found that MVC could achieve lower specific power consumption (kWh/m3) when the cycle was operated under vacuum conditions.

recent_works.title: An economic comparison of wind, solar, and ocean thermal energy in the Federated States of Micronesia
recent_works.abstract: This study provides a thorough economic analysis which compares different renewable energy sources—wind, solar, and open-cycle ocean thermal energy conversion (OC-OTEC)—for generating electric power and freshwater in the Federated States of Micronesia. The novelty of the present work is in developing empirical models for the capital cost as a function of the installed capacity for wind, photovoltaic (PV), and OTEC systems. The analysis incorporates the latest power plant expenses and predicts price variations by considering factors such as capacity and time. In addition, a streamlined method for calculating the necessary battery storage capacity for daily variations in wind and PV solar energy was developed. The OC-OTEC plant was chosen as a case study due to its ability to simultaneously generate energy and produce freshwater, which is crucial for satisfying the energy and freshwater needs of numerous island populations. To provide a fair and equitable comparison, reverse osmosis desalination equipment is integrated into the wind and PV systems. recent_works.title: Comparative Life Cycle Assessment of Landfilling with Sustainable Waste Management Methods for Municipal Solid Wastes
recent_works.abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) generation continues to increase exponentially, leading to the need for better disposal methods. Approximately 50% of the MSW is landfilled in the United States (US). Landfilling is known for its negative effects on the environment and human health. The objective of this study was to conduct a life cycle assessment (LCA) of some of the most common waste treatment methods and propose an alternative and environmentally friendly integrated waste management method (IWM). The LCA was conducted using OpenLCA. Replacing landfilling, incineration, and composting with recycling, gasification, and anaerobic digestion (IWM) reduced the global warming potential from 899 kg CO2 eq to −14.6 kg CO2 eq.
